about.title: About Us
paras: Buganda Investments and Commercial Undertakings Limited (BICUL) aims at generating revenue from engagement in viable appropriate investment and commercial undertakings for financing or co-financing of Buganda’s economic, social and cultural developmental programs.

BICUL takes up its core role of a holding company of the Kingdom that own stake in various companies involved in production of goods & services and preservation of culture for the benefit of the Kingdom.
about.vision: Innovate, empower and create prosperity for Buganda Kingdom.
about.mission: To create Value from the Kingdom’s vast resources.
about.who_text: Buganda Investment and Commercial Undertaking Ltd (BICUL) is the official investment arm of the Buganda Kingdom, committed to building value through land-based investment, partnerships, innovation, and economic empowerment of our people.

why.title: Why Invest in Buganda?
why.lead: The Kingdom of Buganda is the largest traditional Kingdom in present day Uganda, comprising Uganda’s entire Central region including the capital Kampala with the present population of about 10 million people. The Kingdom’s strategic central location is a home of a hive of malleable enterprises, aiding strong commanding investment venture.
why.question: One may wonder, why Buganda
reasons: 70% of business sales or goods and services happen within a radius of 50- 80kms from which is all Buganda.
The passion, love and loyalty of the people of Buganda for their King and Kingdom are in their DNA. You will have guaranteed access to this segment of the market.
The current Kingdom administration is dynamic, empowered engaged and extremely professional
Buganda Kingdom has a lot of land constituted with water, forests and special stones among others
Some pieces of land are in the capital city and urban centers (very prime for high end developments); while the rural areas have big chunks of suitable land for commercial farming.
closing: With the existence of sound macroeconomic policies and a largely attractive investment climate, one is assured of maximizing a decent return on investment more so when they consider partnering with a credible institution that we are.
We welcome you to consider doing business with us.

divisions.title: Statistics Division
divisions.lead: The Statistics Division is the pillar of strong statistical policy and decision making in Buganda Kingdom.
paras: The need for statistical information is recognized as an important and indispensable ingredient of all development programs.
The Statistics Division is governed by appointed board members composed of three eminent Statisticians and three officials from the Kingdom Government:

The legal framework guiding statistical work in Uganda is the Uganda Bureau of Statistics Act (June 1998). This law defines the structure of the National Statistical System (NSS) and the roles of its various players
Uganda Bureau of Statistics (UBOS) appointed Mr. James Muwonge, Director of the Professional Services Unit, as the official Liaison Officer to support and guide the Buganda Statistics Unit.
There is great optimism that with continued support from the Government of Uganda, the donor community, NGOs, and other stakeholders, the Buganda Statistics Division will fully realize its mission.

The Buganda Statistics Unit sincerely thanks all Ministries, Departments, Agencies, and individuals it collaborates with. BSU deeply appreciates their consistent support, cooperation, and encouragement.

divisions.title: Strategic Partnerships Division
divisions.lead: The strategic Partnerships unit was established as department within the Buganda Investment and Commercial Undertaking Limited (BICUL) to attract development partners that are not for profit engagement.
paras: The SPU’s main focus is to research appropriate partnerships and grant opportunities from, private trusts, philanthropic foundations, NGOs and relevant government agencies. The unit seeks to identify and interest donor agencies, creating alliances and inspiring supporters that are willing and seeking to provide funds in form of grants and donations as well as alliances to help Buganda to improve and deliver services to the people at the grass root across all service sectors. In contribution to the strategic plan, the SPU aims at mainly “Creating Wealth and improving the welfare of people living in Buganda. The SPU works in coordination with all Buganda Ministries as delivery channels to service delivery.

divisions.title: Incubation Division
divisions.lead: The Incubation Division is the department holding the fort within Buganda Investments and Commercial Undertaking Limited (BICUL) to incubate ideas and initiatives that are designed to boost the Kingdom’s investment portfolio and equity.
paras: The Incubation Division’s focus is to mainstream engagement in viable appropriate investment and commercial undertakings for financing and/or co-financing of Buganda’s economic, social and cultural development programs. It is an ideation unit which focuses on initiating and receiving, processing and monitoring the implementation of the projects approved by the Kingdom’s Executive structures.

The Division seeks to identify and interest potential investors on the available investment opportunities in pursuit and development of risky business opportunities as we contribute to the achievement of the Kingdom’s Strategic Plan. In coordination with all Buganda ministries and institutions to achieve our mission, the Incubation division is the Kingdom’s platform that tries out new things, offering the ability to face the unknown, to experiment with new ideas, and act with great openness and flexibility.
divisions.vision: To strategically position the Kingdom of Buganda as a key investment partner which focuses on achievement of inclusive sustainable development as it pursues its commitment to take Buganda to the helm.
divisions.mission: To increase the successful development of new businesses and initiatives, job creation and employment in specific sectors that are aligned with the Kingdom’s unique areas of opportunity.
objectives: Preparing and presenting different investment opportunities available in the Kingdom of Buganda to the potential local and international investors.
Engaging in the creation of innovative and sustainable start-up companies/support their growth and development.
Developing and implementing new initiatives for incubation service offerings to potential investment partners and Kingdom companies. Developing new ideas into viable businesses.
Developing and leveraging the Kingdom’s brand for the benefit of the people of Buganda.
Assisting the Kingdom Institutions in proposal writing, pitch deck, business development, fundraising as well as relevant linkages to established companies for business opportunities.
Fostering the entrepreneurial mindset in the Kingdom institutions to drive innovation capabilities.
divisions.summary: Transforming Ideas into Thriving Enterprises to Advance the Kingdom's Growth. We empower startups and entrepreneurial initiatives across diverse sectors through tailored support, strategic investment, and nurturing innovation from seed to scale.

divisions.title: Monitoring and Evaluation
divisions.lead: The Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Office was established under the Partnerships Department within Buganda Investments and Commercial Undertakings Ltd.
paras: Its core mandate is to ensure that all obligations and commitments outlined in the Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) signed between the Buganda Kingdom and her partners are fully implemented and monitored for impact.
This office plays a critical role in fostering mutually beneficial relationships by ensuring that both the Kingdom and her partners derive tangible value from their collaboration.

The Kingdom leverages these partnerships to deliver essential services and development programs to her people, advancing key sectors such as education, health, agriculture, environment, and youth empowerment. Meanwhile, partners benefit from increased visibility, enhanced brand reputation, and positive public relations, as they are seen contributing to meaningful community development initiatives within the Kingdom.

By tracking outcomes and evaluating progress, the M&E Office ensures accountability, learning, and continuous improvements so that the fruits of partnership are not only realized but also sustained for long-term impact.
divisions.summary: Implementing robust systems to track and assess the impact of projects, ensuring accountability and continuous improvement.

impact.heading: Driving Transformation in the Kingdom of Buganda Through Strategic Partnerships

Inspired by our development agenda, “Buganda ku Ntikko” (Buganda at the Helm), we continue to work hand-in-hand with partners from across the globe to design and implement initiatives that uplift communities, preserve culture, and foster inclusive progress.

Buganda has established a network of educational institutions—from nursery to university—offering quality, culturally grounded education.

Nkuluze is referred to as the “Royal Treasury” responsible for taking care of the Kingship. It’s a huge organization within Buganda Kingdom, headed by the Royal Treasurer “Omuwanika w’Enkuluze” (Royal Treasurer). The Royal Treasurer or “Omuwanika w’Enkuluze” is appointed in this office by Ssaabasajja Kabaka and he is only accountable to him. After the 1966 crisis in Buganda, almost all initiatives, undertakings and offices were forcefully closed by the regime including Nkuluze because the King was no longer on the throne (Nnamulondo). However, after the liberation war of 1986, initiatives to reestablish the Kingdom of Buganda started, and so a committee was created to devise means on how the Kingdom would be managed.

The establishment of Muteesa I Royal University (MRU) was both inspired and motivated by Ssabasajja Kabaka Muwenda Mutebi II, with strong support from the Executive Committee of the Buganda Kingdom, led by the Katikkiro. The foundational groundwork was undertaken by the Buganda University Task Force (BUTF), which was inaugurated by the Katikkiro on 8th June 2004 and submitted its final report on 2nd December 2004. Muteesa I Royal University is a chartered university named in honour of Kabaka Muteesa I of Buganda (1856–1884), a visionary monarch whose invitation to Christian missionaries—expressed in a letter to Queen Victoria of England—is widely regarded as the genesis of modern formal education in Uganda.

Lubiri High School opened on 8th February 1999 by the Ministry of Education and Sports Buganda Government Mengo. This was as a result of the need to provide educational services to the people of Buganda and Uganda as a whole. It is located in the Kabaka’s Palace in Mengo. Lubiri High School aims at developing a holistic child through various activities which include sports, technology innovations, entrepreneurship innovations, music, dance and drama. Additionally, the children are involved in community work. They embrace charity programmes within and outside the school. They have continued to visit the sick and shared with the needy spiritually, financially and materially. These activities are redefining the school to change their approaches in order to meet the demands of the 21st century.

At Mwanyi Terimba Limited, we believe that the quality of a coffee brand is defined not just by the taste of the brew, but by the care and passion put into every step of the process. From the farmers who cultivate the beans, to the roasters who unlock their flavors, to the baristas who craft each cup – every hand that touches our coffee shares in our commitment to excellence. This is what sets Mwanyi Terimba apart in a world full of coffee brands.
Buganda Land Board (BLB) is a professional body set up by His Majesty the Kabaka of Buganda to manage land and property returned under the Restitution of Assets and Properties Act of 1993.

Lubiri Nabagereka Nursery and Primary School located inside the Kabaka’s Mengo Palace, with a beautiful evergreen compound which offers a wonderful spacious environment for both academic and co-curricular activities. Nabagereka a Buganda Kingdom owned school was established in the mid-forties to provide basic education to the young children within the palace and its environs under the patronage of Her Royal Highness the Nabagereka as a symbol of her motherly and caring role to the kingdom children. The School was vanquished in the 1966 political crisis when military troops attacked and dethroned Sir Edward Muteesa II.

subsidiaries.name: Buganda Royal Institute of Business and Technical Education (BRIBTE) Mengo

body.x: Buganda Royal Institute of Business and Technical Education (BRIBTE) Mengo was founded by Buganda Kingdom in 1999 with a view to equip students with practical knowledge and skills for employability. The Institute operates under the Ministry of Education, Buganda Kingdom and is registered with the Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES), Central Government. The Institute registration number is PCS/B/144. BRIBTE is also licensed by the National Council for Higher Education (NCHE) to offer training in Business, Technical and Vocational Studies at both Certificate and Diploma levels. In addition, the Institute is recognised by the National Examinations Bodies and was awarded examinations centers from the Uganda Business and Technical Examinations Board (UBTEB), and the Directorate of Industrial Training (DIT).

The Buganda kingdom established BUCADEF in 1994 as a Non-Governmental Organisation (No. S5914/1 432), non political legitimate body corporate particularly charged with spearheading and directing social economic development in communities. It was established to achieve sustainable improvement in the living standards and welfare of the people, in addition building capacities of communities in order to render effective services to cause sustainable development. BUCADEF has various programmes which have been defined and paraded within the overall framework of existing government macro-economic policies and programmes that include;

items: Economic programmes designed to create and expand income earning opportunities, specifically sustainable agriculture and enterprise development, investment and commercial undertakings.
Social sector programmes designed to promote community development, food sufficiency, health and education services, water and sanitation and communal infrastructure.
Social assistance programmes intended to assist disadvantaged social groups.
Production support programmes that support the implementation of the above economic, social and social assistance programmes.

news.title: A team from the Kingdom of Buganda visits Deshiburg Fruits Factory in Luwero

body.x: KAMPALA, UGANDA – 22 January 2026 – Partnerships
A team from the Kingdom of Buganda BICUL & BUCADEF visited Deshiburg Fruits Factory in Luwero, which exports Ugandan canned pineapples worldwide.
The engagement explored partnerships to secure markets for pineapple farmers in Buganda and create jobs for our people.
CEO Mr. Owen revealed the factory will be fully operational in six months and will require at least 500 tonnes of pineapples daily a major opportunity for growers.

news.title: Buganda Kingdom and UNICEF formalise partnership to promote the rights and future of 4.2 million children

body.x: KAMPALA, UGANDA – 13 November 2025 – The Kingdom of Buganda, through the Buganda Investment and Commercial Undertaking Ltd. (BICUL) and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), today signed, at the Buganda Parliament, a pivotal Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to launch a comprehensive partnership dedicated to improving the well-being and fulfilment of rights of the 4.2 million children in the Buganda region.

This collaboration is founded on the conviction that every child deserves to survive, to thrive, and to fulfill their potential. By blending resources with the Kingdom’s deep community roots and cultural authority and UNICEF’s authoritative global technical expertise the partnership is designed to generate sustainable, forward-looking positive change for children.

The spirit of the partnership is intrinsically linked to the traditional Buganda concept of Bulungi Bwansi—working for the common good—reflecting the core principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

At today’s signing event, the Katikkiro of Buganda, Owek. Charles Mayiga highlighted the impact of the collaboration: “The way a community takes care of its children is how its future can be determined. A child is the foundation of adulthood, and we see our responsibility as absolute. We value this collaboration with UNICEF immensely because it enables us to comprehensively ensure child’s health and nutrition, keep children in school, and protect them from violence. Working together allows us to immediately extend our efforts across education, immunization, nutrition, and health, securing the well-being of the next generation of Buganda.”
The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) establishes four interconnected commitments where joint efforts will focus on issues impacting children and their rights, including on:

items: Child survival: Scale up immunization and use Kingdom media to share life-saving information to reduce preventable mortality and malnutrition.
Quality education: Eliminate barriers for vulnerable children. Focus on Early Childhood Development, launch re-enrolment campaigns, and empower Kabaka Youth Councils.
Child protection: End abuse, violence, child marriage, and adolescent pregnancies. Strengthen birth registration systems and collaborate with traditional leaders.

Behaviour change and uplifting children’s voices: Shift attitudes by providing platforms for children to advocate for their own rights, recognizing them as agents of change, and fighting harmful social practices.

body.x: The UNICEF representative, Dr Robin Nandy, noted the urgency and vision of the agreement: “This Memorandum of Understanding is a promise to the children of the Buganda Kingdom and Uganda. We will be a reliable, transparent, and respectful partner, ensuring every resource invested translates into tangible improvements. Together in making a difference for the children, we are greater than the sum of our parts.“

A Joint Steering Committee will be established to define an action plan to implement the commitments taken through the Memorandum of Understanding, monitor progress of activities run and document successful models that can be further scaled up and shared.

news.title: Buganda Kingdom Signs MoU with EACOP to Advance Environmental Conservation and Community Development

body.x: The Kingdom of Buganda is proud to announce the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP) Ltd., aimed at strengthening collaboration in environmental conservation and community development.
This strategic partnership focuses on two key initiatives:

items: 🌳 Advancing tree growing under Ekibira Kya Kabaka
🏟️ Constructing a modern community sports center in Buddu County, Masaka District

body.x: As part of this collaboration, the Kingdom has committed 120 acres of land to support tree growing under the Ekibira Kya Kabaka initiative, and an additional 10 acres for the development of a state-of-the-art sports center. EACOP will provide financial support for the facility, which will serve as a hub for nurturing talent, promoting fitness, and empowering youth through community engagement.

The signing ceremony was held at Bulange Mengo, where our Katikkiro, Owek. Charles Peter Mayiga, emphasized the importance of partnerships that address pressing challenges such as climate change, environmental conservation, and youth empowerment. He stated:

“The Kingdom cherishes partnerships that address urgent challenges such as climate change, environmental conservation, and youth empowerment. Through Ekibira Kya Kabaka and the new community sports center, we are creating a legacy of resilience, opportunity, and growth for our people.”
EACOP’s Managing Director, Mr. Guillaume DULOUT, reaffirmed their commitment to sustainability and socio-economic development, noting:

We were honored by the presence of Hon. Ruth Nankabirwa, Minister of Energy and Mineral Development, who commended both parties for forging a partnership that strengthens environmental conservation and community development.

This collaboration aligns with EACOP’s Social Economic Investment pillars, which prioritize environmental protection and youth empowerment. It also acknowledges the central role of Buganda Kingdom in the pipeline’s journey, with 7 of the 10 pipeline districts located within our territory, covering over 130 villages across four counties.
The Kingdom of Buganda remains steadfast in its commitment to initiatives that uplift our people, protect our environment, and build a resilient future for generations to come.

news.title: Buganda Kingdom signs a Memorandum of Understanding with Uganda Bureau of Statistics (UBOS)

body.x: Uganda Bureau of statistics (UBOS) has formalized a working relationship with Buganda Kingdom aimed at establishing a Buganda statistical unit that will enable an exchange of Statistical data to uphold quality Statistics for the central region.

Uganda Bureau of statistics (UBOS) has formalized a working relationship with Buganda Kingdom aimed at establishing a Buganda statistical unit that will enable an exchange of Statistical data to uphold quality Statistics for the central region. During the signing of the partnership between UBOS and Buganda Kingdom, Buganda Kingdom Premier, Charles Peter Mayiga pledged support to the partnership to ensure collection of data which is accurate and dependable which he said will serve Kabaka’s subjects. While signing the partnership UBOS Executive Director, Dr. Chris Mukiza, highlighted that the high population of Buganda Kingdom of up to 11,453,000 people in 25 districts makes the Kingdom worth of partnering with. He commended the Kabaka for allowing UBOS set up a statistical unit.

“Buganda has a population of 11,453,000 people and it contributes more than 55% to the economy. It has 25 districts and 3 cities. It’s worth to partner with. UBOS will dedicate Senior Statistical officers to work hand in hand with Buganda Kingdom.
Executive Director – UBOS and Buganda Kingdom officials inking the deal

news.title: Buganda Kingdom inked a partnership with Health Hearts Foundation (HHF)

body.x: Buganda Kingdom signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Health Hearts Foundation (HHF) on 17th March 2021, to provide a collaborative platform for co-operation, with an overall objective of prioritizing Primary, Secondary and Tertiary prevention of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) in Uganda and beyond, by improving awareness, early detection, training, advocacy, and access to treatment and Rehabilitation services. The joint partnership will see the provision of a collaborative platform to train, skill, promote, rehabilitate and support the people of Buganda who have been affected by cardiovascular diseases and strokes, and support as many people as possible. The collaboration will increase the resuscitation capacity for primary health workers within the health care facilities, and support cardiovascular advocacy and research programs in Buganda Kingdom and Uganda at large.
Minister for Social Services Buganda Kingdom signing a Memorandum of Understanding with Executive Director Health Heart Foundation

news.title: Affordable houses in Sentema Estate: Buganda Kingdom partners with Centenary Bank

body.x: Buganda Kingdom signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Centenary Rural Development bank on 3rd February 2021, to enable the people acquire affordable housing units in Mirembe estate in Sentema through mortgage financing. Sentema is located only 13 kms from the Kampala Northern By-Pass.

The MoU will see the development of 400 housing units comprising of one to three bedrooms on 50 acres, a vocational school on 10 acres, an industrial park on 50 acres as well as restaurants, shopping mall, clinic and other recreational sites.

news.title: Buganda Kingdom signed a MOU with Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE)

body.x: Buganda Kingdom signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE) on 15th September, 2021 to provide a platform for collaboration and co-operation between the Kingdom of Buganda and Ministry of Water and Environment to foster and advocate for the conservation of water, environment and natural resources.

The joint partnership will see the provision of a collaborative platform to establish a working relationship where the parties would jointly undertake projects/activities relating to Water, Sanitation & Hygiene (WASH) , supporting small and medium scale farmers to use technology for irrigation and livestock watering including water harvesting during the rainy seasons, sustainable utilization of natural resources, and, sensitization on water and environmental protection and conservation.
